sections.context: ADR-0013 makes Creator Onboarding Interview → ProfileGen the reference vertical slice: the one flow built end-to-end so every pattern (auth, db, the @resonance/ai agent+tool registry, streaming UI, Server Actions + Zod, pgvector matching, the full test pyramid) is proven once and future flows are built by replication. It is also the first real backlog for the firstmate-only agentic workflow — decomposed along package boundaries so each step is a self-contained crewmate task in its own worktree.
sections.approach: Build the slice package-by-package, because in this monorepo package boundaries are the parallelization boundaries (ADR-0003) — one step maps to one firstmate crewmate in one treehouse worktree. Foundations first: db schema/migration and core Zod schemas + ports, which everything else consumes. Then ai (Weave interview + ProfileGen agents via the registry, ADR-0009) and ui (streaming Weave rail + Figma profile panels) proceed in parallel against those shared types. Then apps/web wires them with Zod-validated Server Actions behind an authenticated creator session (auth magic-link already landed). Finally an E2E pass proves the flow and seeds the pgvector matching backbone by embedding the generated profile (ADR-0010). Each step ships with its own tests per ADR-0011.

steps.title: db: schema + migration for users, creator_profiles, and profile embeddings
core: Zod schemas, domain types, and ports for interview messages + creator profile
ai: Weave interview agent + ProfileGen agent with saveProfile tool, plus profile embedding
ui: streaming Weave interview rail + generated-profile panels from Figma tokens
web: Zod-validated Server Actions + interview route wiring ui ↔ ai ↔ db behind creator auth
e2e + matching: Playwright flow test end-to-end and pgvector embedding/matching verification

risks: Streaming agent output wired through RSC / Server Actions is fiddly — mismatched streaming contracts between ai and ui can surface only at the web wiring step.
pgvector migration and embedding dimensionality must match the model in @resonance/ai; a dim mismatch fails silently at query time (ADR-0010).
The saveProfile agent tool crosses the ai→db boundary; transaction/ownership boundaries must be explicit so a partial generation cannot persist a half-written profile.
Figma-derived UI can drift from design tokens if built without the Figma MCP context — authorize Figma before the ui step starts.
E2E of a streaming interview is prone to flakiness; the test must assert on settled state, not intermediate tokens.
acceptance: A creator can complete the Weave interview and receive a generated profile persisted to creator_profiles.
The generated profile is embedded into pgvector, proving the matching backbone end-to-end (ADR-0010).
The interview route is gated behind an authenticated creator session.
pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test pass across affected packages, and each package step ships with its own tests (ADR-0011).
A Playwright E2E drives the full flow from front door to generated profile.

sections.context: The deep-module design tenet now lives in .claude/skills/module-design/SKILL.md, but its mapping to Resonance is still marked 'provisional — to be ratified in ADR-0017.' The tenet is not ratified, not indexed for priming, and not enforced at any workflow juncture. So agents designing a package interface, a port/adapter, a query helper, or a component's props have no consistent vocabulary and no explicit depth criterion, and reviews cannot flag a shallow module or a leaky seam. This work formalizes the tenet and weaves it into every point where design happens or design quality is enforced. It is NOT a pivot: it names and makes explicit what Resonance already does implicitly — a @resonance/* package is a module, its src/index.ts entrypoint is a seam, a port is an interface at a seam, and the PGlite/stub fake is the second adapter. The full juncture map and kickoff brief are in docs/module-design-integration-handoff.md; this decomposes the entry-point seed resonance-d279.
sections.approach: Follow the handoff's suggested order as a dependency DAG so every cross-reference points at an already-landed source of truth. ADR-0017 is authored first as the single source of truth and is indexed into mulch the moment it lands; everything else links to it. docs/conventions.md then becomes the operational home — the rules agents actually consult. Those two foundations, in series, unblock a genuinely parallel wave: the root CLAUDE.md pointer line, the four recipe reframings, the planning + prompt-template updates, and the review dimension — each an independent surface depending only on the ADR + conventions. A final verify seed confirms pnpm check:workspace passes, the ADR is indexed, and ml prime surfaces the tenet where an agent would design. Two design tensions from the handoff are resolved INSIDE the ADR (step 1) and treated as acceptance conditions, not afterthoughts: (1) keep 'boundary' for ADR-0003's package/context/ownership sense and introduce 'seam' for the finer-grained location of an interface — a package boundary IS one kind of seam; do NOT rename ADR-0003, add the mapping in the new ADR; (2) justify Resonance's model-ahead ports (StoragePort deferred, PaymentsPort stubbed) as satisfying the two-adapter rule — the test fake is the second adapter and the variance is known/imminent, so 'known future variance + a test fake' counts, while a truly single-adapter, no-known-variance seam is the one to avoid. Chosen over one monolithic edit because the DAG makes the middle wave parallelizable in Phase 2 and prevents dangling forward-references.

sections.context: The reference slice was built mock-first: a runtime RESONANCE_FAKES flag swaps a fake for the live adapter in resolveModel / resolveEmbedder / resolveMail. This kept CI and the full-flow E2E green with zero credentials, but it MASKED live gaps — the Resend transport and the direct-Anthropic/Voyage provider paths were never implemented, yet everything was green, because no test ever exercised a live path. The env-flag fork also lives in shipped runtime code (hard to read) and drifted into a fake-of-a-fake (apps/web/lib/fake-profile-model.ts) because the text-only fake model can't satisfy profile-gen's tool call. ADR-0018 reverses the approach: live-by-default runtime code, fakes injected only in tests, and a credential-gated live-smoke gate so a green build can't hide broken live wiring.
sections.approach: DI-ize the three swap seams (model, embeddings, mail) so shipped code is live-only and every fake is a test-injected dependency, and implement the missing live provider fallbacks so 'live-by-default' actually functions with whatever key is present. The one place a runtime seam was genuinely needed — the full-flow E2E of the running app (you can't DI into a separate server process) — is re-pointed at a credential-gated live-smoke gate rather than a runtime fake. Work package-by-package (ADR-0003): ai + auth seams in parallel, then web removes its fake injection, then the E2E/live-smoke decision, then docs + diagram sync. Fakes move to test-only modules (ai/test, @resonance/db/testing, createFakeMail) that unit/component tests keep using — the fast inner loop stays free and deterministic.

sections.context: The parity audit (design/manifest/) proved the built Creator Interview→ProfileGen UI diverges sharply from the Figma design, while prior seeds (resonance-8329, resonance-0c47, resonance-7d4f) were CLOSED asserting parity that never happened. Root causes: self-certification against docstring node-id citations + a mulch 'design-fidelity pass' record instead of the design itself; provisional tokens laundered into 'done'; and a Figma per-team MCP budget cap (the file sat in a Starter-tier team) that left agents guessing. Concretely: the interview screen is effectively a DIFFERENT design (two narrow bubble cards vs one full-bleed prose conversation with 80px app-nav); the --color-primary ramp is stock Tailwind purple, not Figma indigo #6034ff; and weave-interview-rail's cited node 1443:114245 is the 40px collapsed rail on the Orders screen — a fabricated-in-effect citation. This plan remediates to true, artifact-verified parity.
sections.approach: Anchor every fix to a captured design.png in design/manifest/ under the protocol rules (R2: a claim may only be 'matches design.png except [deltas]', never a bare 'reconciled'; R1: every cited node id must appear in a saved metadata dump; R4: Code Connect makes the node↔component map machine-checked). Sequence: FIRST restore the Figma MCP (reconnect after moving the file to the Pro team) and complete the design-side capture — this gates all design-dependent work — then reconcile screen-by-screen, adopt Code Connect, and record the process learnings so the failure can't recur. NOTE: execution is ON HOLD until the Figma MCP is reconnected (user decision); the plan is authored now so it is claimable the moment the MCP is back.

sections.context:
The member half of the platform (epic resonance-b332) has no entry point: the /start intent picker forks 'exploring/buying' to the scaffold home as an admitted placeholder (intent-form.tsx DESTINATIONS.explore = '/'). Meanwhile the discovery substrate is already live — creator_profiles, the polymorphic embeddings table (vector(1024)), resolveEmbedder(), and findSimilarProfiles all ship today from the ProfileGen slice. Slice A is the smallest shippable member slice that turns that substrate into a product surface: a member (signed in or out) searches, gets embedding-ranked creators, and opens a full profile.

Planning surfaced four facts that correct this seed's original step list. (1) The design has FOUR search frames, none of them in design/manifest: Member/Search/Home (1443:78098) and Member/Search/Result/{Products,Services,Posts,Creators} (1443:78123 / 78133 / 78143 / 78153). Manifest 'screen 07' (1463:71449) is named Onboarding/Creator/SignIn in Figma and is the logged-out member home, not a search screen — the manifest row is mislabeled. (2) The Creators results frame shows result ROWS (avatar, name, Weave badge, 'By <person>', Follow/Following button) behind a Products|Services|Posts|Creators tab bar — not the 'results grid' this seed assumed, and it puts a follow control on the face of the slice. (3) findSimilarProfiles(db, embedding, limit) returns only {id, displayName, headline, similarity} and never filters status='ready', so draft profiles leak into results today; there is no tag filter, threshold, pagination, or by-user lookup. (4) The ADR-0019 capture path is broken: FIGMA_ACCESS_TOKEN returns 403 so all REST tools are dead, and the connected file is vC0O5uyMmw1o5vYHmCoOXq 'Resonance (Copy)' while the manifest's verified fileKey is UYlkCL7jkCVgKWiqAVlEFp. Node ids are preserved at copy time but diverge as the designer keeps editing the original, so citations rot silently — the exact self-certification failure ADR-0019 exists to prevent.
sections.approach:
Build package-by-package because package boundaries are the parallelization boundaries (ADR-0003), and lead with the two things everything else reads: the design contract and the typed discovery contract. Those two are independent of each other, so wave 1 runs them in parallel; db and ui then both build against core's types in wave 2; web composes in wave 3; e2e + pixel-diff parity closes in wave 4.

The central seam is a SWAPPABLE RANKING CONTRACT in @resonance/core (ADR-0017): a small interface — one search method over a Zod-validated query, returning typed creator results — with a deep implementation behind it (embed → filtered ANN SQL → threshold → pagination). Deletion test: delete it and both the web Server Action and the ui row props hand-roll their own query/result shapes, duplicating the contract across two packages, and the resonance-7890 ranking experiments cannot retune thresholds/filters without touching UI. It earns its keep. db implements that interface; web and ui depend only on the interface, never on the SQL.

LOCKED DECISIONS from planning. (a) Build all four designed tabs, with Creators live and Products/Services/Posts as designed empty states — Offering is only {title, description} (no price, image, or product/service type) and @resonance/community is a one-file stub, so three tabs have no data source; shipping the real tab bar keeps the screen structurally faithful and gives Slices B/C obvious sockets. (b) Pull follows FORWARD into Slice A (follows table + follow/unfollow) so the designed Follow/Following control is genuinely functional rather than a visibly dead button; Slice B (resonance-8c96) then owns only member interests + feed assembly, and its description must be updated to match. (c) Build only the results screen at /discover and re-target DESTINATIONS.explore to it — cashing in the placeholder the intent picker deliberately left, so the slice is reachable through the real front door and the E2E can drive /start → search → profile instead of deep-linking. The Member/Search/Home feed shell stays with Slice B, which owns the feed and will add the right-rail search entry then. (d) Figma stays on the Copy for now, but HONESTLY: step 1 records the Copy's fileKey plus a version stamp, flags every new citation copy-derived, and re-plumbs capture onto the plugin bridge since REST is 403. The real fix — read-only against the designer's canonical file, version-pinned captures, writes only ever to a file we own — is filed as a follow-up seed plus an ADR-0019 amendment, because this workflow only ever needs to READ Figma and a copy therefore buys nothing while costing citation integrity. (e) Avatar imagery: creator_profiles has no image column, so result rows ship an initials placeholder logged as an enumerated parity delta, with real imagery filed as a follow-up.

TWO DESIGN CONSTRAINTS inherited by step 3, arising from risk mitigation rather than from the feature itself. First, findSimilarProfiles MUST keep its exact signature: add searchCreatorProfiles as the new deep helper and re-express findSimilarProfiles as a thin wrapper delegating to it, because scripts/verify-live.mjs reads profiles back through it and a rename would break the ADR-0018 live-smoke gate in a credential-gated path CI normally skips. Second, the discovery helper MUST assert embedding.length === 1024 and throw a named ResonanceError before touching SQL, so a dimensionality mismatch fails loudly instead of returning a silently empty result set.

SESSION HANDOFF. No state that matters lives in a conversation: the plan lives in seeds (sd plan show), progress is seed status, discoveries go to mulch with --evidence-seeds, code state is one branch and PR per step, and the reviewed plan-of-record is committed at .lavish/slice-a-plan.html. A cold session reconstructs everything with ml prime / sd prime / sd plan show <pl-id> / sd ready. The wave barriers are the natural resume points — end a session at a barrier with PRs merged rather than carrying a half-built step across it. The worktree fan-out is itself the context strategy: the heavy reading happens in each subagent's context, never in the orchestrating one.

risks: SILENT — Live-smoke gate breaks. scripts/verify-live.mjs asserts a committed profile landed by reading it back through findSimilarProfiles (mulch mx-880c8a); changing that signature breaks the ADR-0018 gate in a credential-gated path CI usually skips. MECHANISM (step 3): do not change the signature at all — add searchCreatorProfiles as the new deep helper and re-express findSimilarProfiles as a thin wrapper delegating to it with its existing shape, so there is one implementation, no drift, and nothing to break. Grep every caller before touching the module; treat the smoke script as part of the public surface. PROOF: the existing verify-live assertion passes untouched.

SILENT — Citation rot from the Figma Copy (vC0O5uyMmw1o5vYHmCoOXq vs the manifest's UYlkCL7jkCVgKWiqAVlEFp). Node ids resolve in both but diverge in meaning as the designer edits the original, so a cited id silently stops matching the frame it names. MECHANISM (step 1): REST is 403 so Figma version ids are unavailable — instead every new design.md records fileKey, nodeId, capture timestamp, a SHA-256 of the captured design.png, and provenance: copy-derived, making a changed frame detectable by hash alone with no REST access. Add design/manifest/PROVENANCE.md stating plainly which file the manifest currently trusts and why. PROOF: re-running capture reproduces identical hashes.

SILENT — Embedding dimensionality drift. Dims are pinned at 1024 (Voyage voyage-3.5); a mismatch fails at query time without erroring (ADR-0010). MECHANISM (step 3): assert embedding.length === 1024 at the seam and throw a named ResonanceError before touching SQL, converting a silent empty result into an immediate explicit failure; use only resolveEmbedder(), never a second client. PROOF: a unit test feeding a wrong-length vector asserts the throw rather than an empty array.

BLOCKING — REST-path assumption stalls a subagent. The manifest's own capture notes document download_assets / get_file_data, both now 403. MECHANISM (step 1): rewrite the 'Capture notes' section of design/manifest/README.md with the working Desktop Bridge procedure (figma_capture_screenshot / figma_execute) and state the REST status explicitly. Step 1 gates step 4 in the DAG so the UI agent cannot start before the notes are correct. PROOF: step 4 captures without needing help.

CONFUSING — Pre-existing status leak misleads debugging. Missing status='ready' filtering is a live correctness bug today, so 'wrong results' may predate this slice. MECHANISM (step 3): land the status filter as the opening commit, before the new search surface exists, pinned by a draft-profile fixture — after that commit any bad result is definitionally this slice's doing. PROOF: the draft-fixture test fails against the old query and passes against the new one.

REWORK — Slice B double-builds follows. resonance-8c96 still lists the follows table; left unedited it gets built twice and the migrations collide. MECHANISM (step 3): edit the sibling seed inside the step that steals its work rather than at the end of the slice — updating resonance-8c96's description is part of step 3's definition of done, so the follows table and the scope edit land together or not at all. PROOF: sd show resonance-8c96 no longer claims follows.

POLISH — Empty states read as breakage. Three tabs are permanently empty this slice; vague copy makes the screen look broken rather than incomplete. MECHANISM (step 4): copy signed off in review, and an RTL test renders the dataless-tab state and the zero-result state and asserts they are distinguishable, so the distinction cannot regress into identical blanks. PROOF: RTL test asserting two distinct states.

RESOLVED IN REVIEW — Avatar imagery vs designed thumbnails. creator_profiles has no avatar/image column but the designed rows show thumbnails. DECISION: ship the initials placeholder, log it as an enumerated delta so the parity statement stays honest ('matches design.png except [avatar imagery]'), and file real creator imagery as a follow-up seed. No longer an open question.
acceptance: A member — signed in or signed out — can pick 'exploring/buying' at /start, land on /discover, type a query, and get embedding-ranked creators; draft-status profiles never appear in results.

The results screen renders the designed Products|Services|Posts|Creators tab bar with Creators live and the other three showing designed empty states that are visually distinct from a zero-result search.
A signed-in member can follow and unfollow a creator from a result row and the Follow/Following state persists across reload; a signed-out member is prompted rather than silently failing.
Opening a creator from a result row shows their full profile including offerings rendered on /creator/[id].

Ranking is swappable behind the @resonance/core discovery contract: db implements the interface, and web/ui import only the interface — verified by an implementation swapped in tests, so resonance-7890 can retune without touching UI or actions.

design/manifest has rows and design.png artifacts for the four Member/Search frames, the mislabeled screen 07 row is corrected, every new citation records the fileKey + version stamp it came from and is flagged copy-derived, and the bridge-based capture path is documented.
/discover parity is stated as a diff of two images per ADR-0019 — 'matches design.png except [deltas]' with deltas enumerated — never as a prose claim, with unverified values marked PROVISIONAL.
A Playwright E2E drives /start → search → ranked results → creator profile end to end, asserting on settled state rather than intermediate tokens.

pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test pass across affected packages, each step ships its own tests (ADR-0011), scripts/verify-live.mjs still passes its findSimilarProfiles assertion, and pnpm check:workspace is green.

sections.context: The designer delivered five specs (Evolution Engine, Pattern Registry, Interaction Philosophy v1.2, Interaction Principles, Emerging Creator Onboarding Flow v1.1) describing a self-auditing behavioral system for Weave. The codebase can host none of it today. Weave's behavior is two hardcoded TypeScript string literals (CREATOR_INTERVIEW_SYSTEM, PROFILE_GEN_SYSTEM) with no version, no structure, no provenance, and no relationship to the philosophy and principles the designer has authored. Separately, the product captures ZERO observations: the interview transcript is ephemeral client state by explicit design decision, there is no telemetry, no analytics, and no evaluation scoring anywhere in the repo. Both halves of the Evolution Engine are therefore blocked — there is nothing structured to evolve, and no evidence to evolve it from. This slice lands exactly those two foundations: a versioned, validated, repo-governed behavioral corpus behind a resolver seam, and an evidence-capture seam that takes simulated runs now and production observations later. The five engine agents (Evaluator, Researcher, Architect, Validator, Evolution Manager) are explicitly OUT of scope and get their own plan once this shape exists to build against.
sections.approach:
Codebase architecture takes precedence over the spec's proposed structure; the spec's paths are treated as placeholders throughout.

CORPUS AS REPO DATA, COMPILED AT BUILD. The corpus is authored as YAML in a new @resonance/weave-os package, schema-validated and compiled into typed frozen objects at build time. No runtime filesystem reads (ADR-0002, and Vercel bundling makes fs reads fragile). This rejects the spec's standalone weave-evolution-engine/ repo tree, which conflicts with ADR-0003 package boundaries.

GOVERNANCE IS GIT, NOT A NEW SUBSYSTEM. Spec section 16's file-safety rules (approved/candidate separation, visible diff, no self-approval, rollback) are already provided by git + PR + the no-mistakes gate. Spec section 17's versioning (file version, release version, approval record, rollback reference) is provided by commits and tags. We build neither. We add exactly two things git cannot express: a CODEOWNERS file encoding section 15's approval-authority tiers (WHO must approve), and consumption of each file's authored evolution_policy block (WHAT counts as a valid reason to change it). The philosophy file's unacceptable_reasons — 'temporary performance improvement', 'easier implementation', 'stylistic preference' — are the anti-Goodhart guardrail that stops a future score-optimizing agent loop from eroding the foundation, and they must be enforced in code rather than honored in prose.

THE RESOLVER IS THE DEEP MODULE (ADR-0017). One small interface — resolveWeaveOs({ flow, context }) -> { system, flow, outputs, releaseId } — over a large implementation: parse, validate, resolve inheritance, route, activate, compose, stamp. It deliberately returns four things because the corpus contains three different KINDS of content, and collapsing them into one system prompt would build the wrong thing: guidance and copy compose into the prompt today; machinery (flow_map, optional_branches, session_state, captures, actions) is typed and validated but NOT yet consumed by the current free-form runtime; output constraints are validation input for generation. The measurable gap between what the corpus specifies and what the runtime implements is a deliberate, tracked artifact — it is what the Evaluator will later score against.

INHERITANCE NORMALIZED CHILD-SIDE. The designer writes inheritance both directions: parent-side (philosophy's architecture.inherited_by) and child-side (the flow file's inherits). Storing it parent-side would mean every new root file requires editing the most-protected file in the system (change_threshold: exceptional). We store the edge child-side and render inherited_by as a derived view, preserving his mental model.

THE PATTERN REGISTRY SPLITS IN TWO. The rulebook (promotion targets, thresholds, metric definitions, pattern schema) is stable config and lives as repo YAML. The pattern and evidence records accumulate, are queried, and link to observations by foreign key — that is application data and lives in Postgres via @resonance/db. This satisfies both the spec's own constraint (inherited_by_runtime: false) and the repo rule that every read/write goes through @resonance/db. Promotion produces a PR against the corpus, which is where section 16's governance actually needs to bite.

EVIDENCE SEAM COPIES DiscoveryPort EXACTLY. Interface in @resonance/core, live adapter in @resonance/db, consumers depend on the interface and never on SQL — the pattern already proven by DiscoveryPort/createDiscoveryAdapter. That is what makes 'simulated now, production later' a one-line adapter swap rather than a rewrite. Every observation is stamped with the OS release id, and the release is PINNED AT CONVERSATION START so an in-flight interview cannot shift mid-conversation and evidence stays attributable.

SCORING RUBRIC COMES FREE. The Principles doc's 7 records each carry prioritize/avoid lists that are directly checkable against a transcript. Cross-referencing with Evolution Engine section 11 shows the 7 principles and the 10 evaluation dimensions are different lists that COMPOSE: 'principle_alignment' is one dimension that decomposes into 7 sub-scores, and the other 9 are process/outcome measures. The Evaluator therefore scores 16 things, not 10, and we do not invent the criteria.

RUNNER BOUNDARY — REQUEST-SCOPED vs JOB-SCOPED (added at plan review). ADR-0009's 'one shared runner' is scoped to request-time product agents and stays as-is. It cannot serve the Evolution Engine: runAgentStream returns an HTTP stream and runAgentStructured is hard-capped at stopWhen stepCountIs(1), so neither can drive a multi-turn agentic loop. The engine needs a job-scoped executor — multi-step Architect reasoning, a human-in-the-loop pause spanning days, fan-out over test cases, resume-without-re-billing, and record-and-continue partial-failure semantics instead of the runner's fail-fast throw. ADR-0009 anticipated exactly this in its 'When to revisit (add Vercel Workflow / WDK)' section; the engine trips three of its five named triggers (#2 expensive re-run, #4 human-in-the-loop pause, #5 fan-out/fan-in). Adding a third runAgentLoop entry point to runner.ts would conflate two different altitudes behind one shallow interface and is rejected. This slice does NOT design the executor — that would repeat the 'designing blind' failure we avoided by deferring the five agents. Instead: step 2's ADR records the boundary and names the tripped triggers, leaving the design open; step 6 builds the multi-turn conversation driver the simulated harness genuinely requires, which becomes the deliberate design spike for the engine's executor (the same move as using corpus transcription to spike the Architect).

alternatives.name: Corpus stored in Postgres with an in-app approval UI
alternatives.rejected_because: Lets non-engineers approve without a PR, but rebuilds versioning, diffing, candidate separation, and approval from scratch when git already provides all four. Revisit only if non-engineer authorship becomes a hard blocker.

alternatives.name: Runtime YAML reads from the filesystem, as the spec's tree implies
alternatives.rejected_because: Loses build-time validation, is fragile under Vercel bundling, and pushes parse cost into every request.

alternatives.name: Resolver returns a single composed system prompt string
alternatives.rejected_because: Simplest interface, but silently discards the machinery half of the active file (stages, branches, session_state, captures) and would force a second parse elsewhere. A shallow interface over a deep problem.

alternatives.name: Standalone weave-evolution-engine repository per spec section 18
alternatives.rejected_because: Conflicts with ADR-0003 package boundaries and would fork the toolchain, test pyramid, and CI.

alternatives.name: Build the five engine agents in this slice
alternatives.rejected_because: They would be designed against a corpus and evidence shape that does not exist yet, guaranteeing rework. Deferred to a follow-on plan.

alternatives.name: Regression-gate the prompt change on strict behavioral equivalence to today's literals
alternatives.rejected_because: Assumed the corpus would describe current behavior. It does not — the flow spec is a forward design (11 stages vs. free-form chat). Replaced with an explicit reviewed prompt diff.

steps.title: core: Weave OS corpus contracts + ObservationPort + the 16 evaluation dimensions
adr: ratify the Weave OS architecture + the request/job-scoped runner boundary; CODEOWNERS; amend ADR-0009 + ADR-0016
weave-os: new package — transcribe the corpus, loader, cross-file validator, resolver seam
db: observations + evaluation_scores + pattern records, migration, and the live ObservationPort adapter
ai: resolver-fed agent definitions, retire the prompt literals, pin the release, emit observations
evolution: new package — simulated-run harness + the multi-turn conversation driver (first job-scoped executor)
web: pin the OS release per conversation, wire the observation adapter, sync the architecture diagram

risks: TRANSCRIPTION AUTHORITY DRIFT: a transcribed or derived corpus looks authoritative and is easier for the designer to accept than to rewrite, so our normalization quietly becomes his philosophy. Mitigation: every record carries an explicit source and confidence field reusing his own ladder (design_hypothesis..high_confidence); the corpus reaches him as a reviewed PR diff, not a finished artifact; nothing is invented to fill a gap.

UNRESOLVED CROSS-FILE REFERENCES: the flow file's applied_principles names seven ids (expression_before_positioning, creator_sovereignty, discovery_over_directive, low_cognitive_load, reflection_not_interpretation, provisional_identity, relational_not_marketing_language) that do not exist in the Principles doc's seven records. Two vocabularies. This MUST fail validation loudly and go back to the designer — silently mapping or inventing the missing principles would corrupt the foundation on day one.

SCOPE LEAK INTO THE STAGED INTERVIEW: the flow spec describes an 11-stage machine with session_state, typed captures, depth modes, and 3-candidate outputs that the runtime does not implement. This slice types and validates that machinery but must NOT start consuming it. If flow consumption creeps in, the slice becomes a full interview rebuild.

SILENT BEHAVIOR CHANGE ON PROMPT RETIREMENT: swapping the two literals for a composed prompt can change interview and ProfileGen behavior in ways tests do not catch. Mitigation: snapshot the currently-shipped prompts, produce an explicit composed-vs-current diff, and require reviewed sign-off rather than a claim of equivalence.

DEFECTIVE SOURCE DOCUMENTS: all five specs are Google Docs exports with escaped underscores; the philosophy file duplicates source_of_truth (lines 247-248), disagrees with Engine section 4 on the heuristics filename, and contains a garbled belief at line 233 ('Stories carry emotions, clarify emotions serve creators'). Transcription must log every defect for designer resolution and must never guess intent.

MEMBER-SIDE SCOPE WITH NO SOURCE: the OS was scoped to cover creator AND member surfaces, but no member active file exists in any spec and /discover is search rather than conversation. Risk of inventing member content. Explicitly excluded from v0; tracked as a follow-up.

TWO NEW PACKAGES: increases workspace surface and boundary-lint scope. pnpm check:workspace, the boundary lint, and the Turbo graph must stay green; both packages ship their own CLAUDE.md declaring real-vs-pending status per repo convention.

REGISTRY SPLIT IS A JUDGMENT CALL: putting evidence records in Postgres while the rulebook stays in YAML is our synthesis, not the designer's stated design. If he expects one hand-editable file, this needs renegotiation before the db step lands.
acceptance: resolveWeaveOs({ flow: 'emerging_creator_onboarding', context }) returns a composed system prompt, a typed flow definition, typed output constraints, and a stable release id — sourced from the corpus, with zero runtime filesystem reads.

Interaction Philosophy v1.2, Interaction Principles (7 records), and Emerging Creator Onboarding Flow v1.1 are transcribed into schema-valid YAML, each record carrying source and confidence provenance.
The cross-file validator FAILS on the seven unresolved applied_principles references and names each one — proving reference validation works rather than papering over the conflict.
Every defect found in the source documents is recorded in a defect log for the designer; none is silently corrected.
CREATOR_INTERVIEW_SYSTEM and PROFILE_GEN_SYSTEM are retired; the composed-vs-shipped prompt diff is produced and explicitly signed off (not asserted equivalent).
The OS release id is pinned at conversation start and stamped onto every observation, so an in-flight interview cannot shift release mid-conversation.
The simulated harness runs at least one creator persona through at least one flow end-to-end, producing observation records and evaluation-dimension scores written through ObservationPort.

Evaluation scoring covers 16 dimensions: 7 principle sub-scores (using each principle's authored prioritize/avoid lists as the rubric) plus the 9 remaining process/outcome dimensions from Evolution Engine section 11.
The nine Pattern Registry patterns are present in the corpus as INACTIVE records carrying their registry ids as provenance — addressable and promotable, but not inherited into any runtime prompt.

An ADR ratifies: repo-versioned corpus compiled at build, the resolver seam and its four-part return, the registry split, child-side inheritance normalization, and governance via CODEOWNERS plus evolution_policy — each with an explicit note where it overrides the designer's spec and why.
CODEOWNERS encodes Evolution Engine section 15's approval tiers (flow-local, behavior rule, heuristic, principle/philosophy, new root module).
The architecture diagram is updated with both new packages and the corpus + observation data flows, and its SVG/PNG outputs are regenerated (ADR-0015).
No member-side corpus content is authored; the gap is filed as a follow-up seed.
pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test are green, pnpm check:workspace is green, and package-boundary lint passes with no cross-internal imports.

sections.context:
Slice A shipped member discovery as a search-driven surface: /discover ranks creators by embedding similarity to a typed query, with follow/unfollow live. But a member who has just signed up and typed nothing sees a plain idle empty state — the platform knows nothing about them, so it can suggest nothing. The parent epic (resonance-b332, locked decision 4) puts a lightweight member interest-picker in Slice B as the counterpart to the creator interview: the creator tells Weave what they offer, the member tells us what they care about, and both become vectors in the same pgvector space so the two sides can be matched.

The design already answers what this looks like. Member/Onboarding/CreateAccount/Selection (Figma vC0O5uyMmw1o5vYHmCoOXq node 1554:79520) draws 'Select 3 topics' over a grid of Tag chips, subtitled 'We will suggest creators and offerings resonate with you', with a Continue button — placed inside the member signup flow after email verification. The seed's claim that new Figma frames are needed is wrong for the picker: it exists and is buildable today on the Tag primitive @resonance/ui already ships.

What the design does NOT support is a separate personalized feed surface. Both Member/Onboarding/Home (1443:78391) and Member/Search/Home (1443:78098 — whose captured spec explicitly assigns the screen to Slice B) draw the logged-in home as a POST feed: a 710px centre column of Post cards with a 'What's on your mind?' composer, beside a Cart right rail. @resonance/community holds a Post type and nothing else; the composer, posts, likes and the cart are all Slice C (resonance-537e). Building that frame now would ship a dead surface — the exact outcome rejected in Slice A planning, which is why the follows table was pulled forward rather than shipping a dead Follow control.
sections.approach:
Ship the interests capability and spend it on the surface that already exists, rather than opening a new one. Members pick topics during signup; those topics become an 'interest' embedding; /discover's empty-query state becomes an interest-ranked list of creators instead of a blank idle message. No /feed route, no Post card, no composer, no cart — @resonance/community is untouched by this slice.

The architectural centre of the slice is that personalization goes BEHIND the existing ranking seam, not beside it. DiscoveryPort (@resonance/core) is documented as THE swappable ranking seam: one method, behind which sits embed-query, status filter, ANN search, tag filter, threshold, keyset pagination and follow-state resolution. 'Rank by the viewer's stored interest vector when there is no query text' is another ranking strategy, so it belongs in that implementation. The only interface change is that DiscoveryQuerySchema.text — today a required z.string().trim().min(1) — becomes optional, because the current contract literally cannot express 'no query, rank me by my interests'. DiscoveryPort keeps exactly ONE method. Interface unchanged in shape, implementation deeper: the ADR-0017 deletion test still passes, and resonance-7890's future ranking experiments inherit the new branch for free.

Interest WRITES deliberately do not go on DiscoveryPort, following the precedent the port already sets for follow mutation ('Follow mutation is deliberately not here — it is not ranking'). They ship as direct @resonance/db exports, exactly as followCreator/unfollowCreator did in Slice A.

Topics are a curated list seeded into a real topics table rather than a hardcoded constant, so the taxonomy can be edited and extended later without a migration. The seed values are the labels the frame draws, deduplicated: the design's chip grid contains 'Art' twice (14 chips, 13 unique).

Decomposition follows package boundaries (ADR-0003), which are the parallelization boundaries: core contracts first, then db and ui in parallel against them, then web wires the two, then E2E proves the flow.

alternatives.name: Build the designed Post feed and pull the composer forward from Slice C
alternatives.rejected_because: Highest design fidelity, but it requires a posts table, feed assembly, the Post card composite AND the post composer — all of which are Slice C scope (resonance-537e). Without the composer the feed ships dead, which Slice A planning explicitly rejected. This would absorb a large part of the next vertical into this one.

alternatives.name: New /feed route listing creators and offerings, reusing CreatorResultRow
alternatives.rejected_because: Matches the epic's 'discovery-ranked for you feed' wording literally, but creates a brand-new surface whose centre column knowingly contradicts the frame that governs it — a permanent enumerated ADR-0019 delta on a screen we chose to create. It delivers no capability that interest-ranking the existing /discover surface does not already deliver.

alternatives.name: A separate InterestsPort owning personalized ranking
alternatives.rejected_because: Splits ranking across two seams and directly contradicts DiscoveryPort's stated rationale as the one swappable ranking seam. resonance-7890's ranking experiments would then have to be implemented twice.

alternatives.name: Derive the topic chips from tags already present on published creator profiles
alternatives.rejected_because: Self-maintaining and guarantees every topic maps to real supply, but the picker's contents would then vary with the data and would not match the 13 topics the frame draws. Rejected for Slice B; worth revisiting when the catalogue is large enough that the curated list goes stale.

alternatives.name: Require exactly 3 topics before Continue enables
alternatives.rejected_because: The design's literal reading, and it would guarantee every member has an interest vector. Rejected because it is a hard gate on the signup front door; skippable keeps the door open and forces the no-interests fallback to be a real, tested path rather than an assumption.

steps.title: core: Topic + MemberInterests contracts, and make DiscoveryQuery.text optional so the ranking seam can express 'rank me by my interests'
db: topics + member_interests tables and migration, curated topic seed, 'interest' embedding, and the interest-ranked branch of the discovery adapter
ui: TopicPicker composite built from Figma 1554:79520 on the existing Tag primitive, verified by pixel diff
web: member signup topic step + Zod-validated Server Action, and /discover's empty-query surface rendering interest-ranked creators
e2e: Playwright drives pick-topics -> personalized /discover, and the skip path -> today's idle surface

risks: Relaxing DiscoveryQuerySchema.text from required to optional loosens a validation boundary on untrusted client input. 'Absent' and 'empty string' must stay distinguishable — a whitespace-only search must still fail validation rather than silently becoming a personalized browse. The adapter must return an empty page for a viewer with no interests, never an unranked dump of every creator.

The interest embedding must be produced by the same embedder and dimensionality as creator-profile embeddings or cosine similarity between them is meaningless (ADR-0010). resonance-e0e6 is already open on EMBEDDING_DIMS not being converged onto the shared @resonance/core constant; this slice must not add a third place that hardcodes it.

The design's chip grid lists 'Art' twice — 14 chips, 13 unique labels. The seed must dedupe, and the duplication should be confirmed with the designer rather than silently 'fixed', in case two distinct topics were intended.

This slice edits the member signup flow, which is the same front door the E2E harness drives. The cold-start OTP race (resonance-86dd) was only just fixed by making the harness mail singleton promise-pinned; adding another parallel auth-adjacent request in signup could reintroduce a concurrency bug in that path.

Because the picker is skippable, the 'no interests' branch is a real production path, not an edge case. If it is left untested, a signed-in member who skipped could see an error or an unranked dump where today they see a clean idle surface.

Slice B deliberately does not build the designed member home (Member/Search/Home 1443:78098), whose captured spec assigns the screen to this slice. Screen 08 stays orphan-design with no parity claim. This must be stated explicitly in design/manifest, or a later reviewer will read /discover's populated empty-query surface as a parity regression against a frame it was never trying to match.

Topic selection is identity-adjacent data written from a Server Action. The member must come from the session, never from the payload — the same rule Slice A's discovery actions follow, where the viewer is a separate parameter with no spoofable field on the query.
acceptance: A new member can select topics during signup and the selection persists; skipping is possible and leaves the member with no interests rather than a partial or failed write.
Selected topics are embedded into the embeddings table with sourceType 'interest' keyed to the user, using the same embedder and dimensionality as creator-profile embeddings.
/discover with no query text ranks published creators by similarity to the viewer's interest vector; with no interests, or signed out, it renders today's idle surface unchanged.
DiscoveryPort still exposes exactly one method. The personalized ranking lives behind the seam, and the in-test fake adapter drives the new no-text branch through the same contract (ADR-0017).
A whitespace-only or empty-string query still fails validation at the boundary rather than being treated as a personalized browse.
The TopicPicker matches design.png for node 1554:79520 except explicitly enumerated deltas, verified by pixel diff per ADR-0019.
design/manifest records that screen 08 (Member/Search/Home) remains orphan-design and is NOT claimed by this slice, with the reason.
@resonance/community is untouched: no posts table, no feed assembly, no Post card, no composer.
pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test pass across affected packages, each package step ships its own tests (ADR-0011), and a Playwright E2E drives both the pick-topics path and the skip path.

name: Slice B — Member interests personalize discovery

sections.context:
After the member-interests work, /interests sits between email verification and the rest of onboarding for EVERY newly verified account, and unconditionally continues to /onboarding/creator. Members should reach /discover instead, but the app cannot tell a member from a creator at that point: setUserRoles is never called from app code, the roles column defaults to "member", and nothing ever writes "creator" except commitCreatorProfile at the very end of the creator interview.

The deeper problem is that the /start intent is not data. Routing is only the first surface to need it; creator-only screens, the Member/TurnToCreator conversion, and analytics all need to know what someone came here to do. Jared decided to make it real data rather than merely move the destination.

A collision surfaced while reading the code, and it is what shaped this plan. commitCreatorProfile writes the role LAST on purpose, and its comment states the invariant plainly: a member only becomes a creator once a discoverable profile and embedding are durably persisted. Writing "creator" at signup would contradict that outright. Nothing gates on roles today (the only reader in the repo is commitCreatorProfile reading currentRoles to append to), so the contradiction would be invisible — which is exactly why it would be inherited, unexamined, by the first surface that does gate on it.

The resolution keeps the two concepts apart entirely: "creator" stays an EARNED status meaning the creator onboarding was completed, and the thing recorded at the fork is the INTENT, in its own column.
sections.approach:
Store the /start intent as its own durable field. Do NOT widen the role enum.

A new nullable column, user.onboarding_intent, holds the closed enum explore | share | business. RoleSchema is untouched, so "creator" keeps meaning exactly what commitCreatorProfile already guarantees — the creator onboarding was completed and a discoverable profile exists. Roles stay an authorization concept; a point in an onboarding journey is not a role.

Storing the intent rather than a creator_pending role value also KEEPS INFORMATION the role approach would have thrown away: /start draws three intents and the design forks share from business, but both collapse to a single "pending creator" role. The column preserves the distinction at no extra cost, and that distinction is most of the analytics value that motivated making this real data in the first place.

The intent reaches the fork as a closed enum in the URL: /signup?intent=share, threaded into the magic-link callbackURL and through the OTP path, parsed with Zod at /interests. This is materially unlike the next-URL threading already declined — that was a free-form redirect target needing an allowlist, this is a closed three-value enum that is never used as a URL. The worst an attacker does by forging it is send themselves down an onboarding path /start offers for free.

Routing reads the parsed URL value, which is authoritative at that moment; the column is written in the same action so the fact survives the request. The web shell holds neither rule: the write is setOnboardingIntent in @resonance/db (ADR-0002), which is also the seam the TurnToCreator conversion calls later so a second writer never appears.

The column is deliberately NOT declared in Better Auth's additionalFields. Nothing in the auth flow reads it, so it stays out of the session payload and out of Better Auth's surface — it is our column on their table, written and read through Drizzle.

The enum type lives in @resonance/core, which packages/ui already depends on, so ui's local OnboardingIntent union re-points to it with no new package edge and no architecture-diagram change. A nullable column on an existing table is not a change to the system's shape, so ADR-0015 does not call for a diagram update either.

Compared with the creator_pending variant this replaces, the plan gets SMALLER: @resonance/ai is untouched (commitCreatorProfile keeps appending "creator" exactly as it does today, and re-commit stays a no-op), which removes a step, and the whole class of enum-widening rollout risk disappears with it.

alternatives.name: Add creator_pending to RoleSchema (the previous revision of this plan)
alternatives.rejected_because: Jared's call on review, and correct: "being a creator" implies having gone through creator onboarding, so a not-yet-a-creator state does not belong in the role enum. It also forces every future consumer of roles to decide which values it accepts, and it collapses share and business into one value, discarding a distinction the design draws and the analytics case wants. Its only advantage was avoiding a migration.

alternatives.name: creator means "on the creator path" (write member,creator at the fork)
alternatives.rejected_because: Smallest diff, but it silently breaks the invariant commitCreatorProfile documents and orders its writes around — a user who abandons the interview would read as a creator. Nothing gates on roles today, so the breakage would sit invisible until the first surface that does.

alternatives.name: httpOnly signed cookie set at /start
alternatives.rejected_because: No URL surface at all, but ambient and invisible: harder to drive from Playwright and to reproduce by hand, for a value whose forged worst case is choosing your own onboarding path. It also solves only routing, leaving nothing durable behind.

alternatives.name: Write the intent at verification instead of at the /interests fork
alternatives.rejected_because: Moves where the write happens without answering how the intent travels — it still needs the URL enum to get that far. Jared confirmed the column is for routing and conversion, not for measuring signup-time intent, so the fork is the right place.

alternatives.name: Build the Member/TurnToCreator conversion screen in this plan
alternatives.rejected_because: Widens the plan by a route, a Figma-derived component and an E2E spec beyond the decided scope. setOnboardingIntent is built as the shared seam so the conversion calls it later; filed as a follow-up seed instead.

steps.title: core: own the OnboardingIntent enum as the single definition
ui: re-point OnboardingIntent at the core enum so one definition remains
db: add the user.onboarding_intent column + setOnboardingIntent, the TurnToCreator seam
web: carry the /start intent through both verify channels, persist it, fork /interests
e2e: assert member intent lands on /discover and creator intent on /onboarding/creator

risks: THE TWO-CHANNEL TRAP, the likeliest way to ship this half-broken: the intent must survive BOTH the magic-link callback and the OTP path. signup-form must thread it into callbackURL AND into the /verify?email= push, or a member who clicks the link lands somewhere different from one who types the code. The existing AFTER_VERIFY constants are duplicated in signup-form and verify-form precisely because those two must never diverge; the intent now inherits that same requirement. Assert it per channel, not once.

This adds a real SQL migration where the previous revision needed none. The column must be NULLABLE with no default: every existing user predates the fork, null honestly means "never went through /start", and no backfill is correct or required. Use the add-db-migration recipe so schema, migration and generated SQL stay consistent (ADR-0004, ADR-0010).

The column sits on Better Auth's user table but is deliberately NOT declared in additionalFields. Whoever implements the db step must not add it there reflexively for symmetry with roles — roles is declared because getSession decodes it into SessionUser; the intent is not read by the auth flow and must stay out of the session payload.

A creator-intent user who abandons at /interests never gets an intent recorded, since the write happens at the fork. Jared confirmed this is fine: the column is for routing and conversion, not for measuring signup-time intent. It is recoverable because /start can be re-entered.

Routing reads the parsed URL value rather than reading the column back, so a forged param changes only that user's own destination — an onboarding path /start offers for free. An absent, unknown or malformed value must degrade to member rather than throw.

Playwright specs share a dev database and Better Auth allows one account per email. Every spec that signs up needs its afterEach account cleanup, which is what stopped the earlier fixture-leak class; adding an intent variant means MORE accounts per run, not fewer.
The no-mistakes gate cannot run a browser E2E in this repo and will raise it as a finding. Expect it and decide it once — the browser evidence comes from CI, which injects DATABASE_URL.
acceptance: RoleSchema is UNCHANGED, and @resonance/ai is untouched: commitCreatorProfile still appends "creator" exactly as it does today and re-commit is still a no-op.
OnboardingIntentSchema lives in @resonance/core and is the single definition; packages/ui's OnboardingIntent is that type, not a second union.
user.onboarding_intent exists as a nullable column with no default, added through the add-db-migration recipe, and is NOT declared in Better Auth's additionalFields.
setOnboardingIntent in @resonance/db is the only app-reachable write for the column, validates through OnboardingIntentSchema, and is idempotent.
The /start intent survives BOTH verification channels: a member who clicks the magic link and one who types the OTP reach the same destination, asserted for each channel.
An absent, unknown or forged intent param degrades to member — no throw, no 500, nothing written.
/interests continues to /discover for a member and to /onboarding/creator for a creator intent, asserted in Playwright for both, with the intent persisted in the same action.
share and business are stored distinctly rather than collapsed, so the design's two creator intents remain distinguishable.
The three existing E2E specs still pass, each deleting the account it creates in afterEach.
pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test pass, and every child seed shipped through its own no-mistakes gate.
A follow-up seed exists for the Member/TurnToCreator conversion (Figma 1443:78478) calling setOnboardingIntent.
